about: The epistle of the Third Sunday of Advent, from which the day takes its name of Gaudéte. The call to rejoice stands beside a call to modesty and to freedom from anxiety — three things Paul binds together because “the Lord is nigh”.

s01.translation: Brethren: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s02.translation: Let your gentleness be known to all people; the Lord is near.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s03.translation: Be anxious about nothing, but in every prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, make your petitions known to God.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s04.translation: And may the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus our Lord.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition
